- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in the history (e.g., after 80+ values), then undercorrects or lags in subsequent days.
- Underestimates in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, suggesting mean reversion or failure to capture late-period momentum.
- Forecasts tend to be too smooth; fails to capture volatility clustering or sudden drops after spikes.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to recent price increases — often takes 2–3 days to adjust upward.
- Overconfident in early forecast days; should reduce initial forecast magnitude by 2–5% relative to recent history mean.
- When history shows strong upward momentum, model should apply a “safety margin” to avoid overestimating peak prices.
- Avoid extrapolating linear trends; price corrections often occur in non-linear fashion, especially after 80+ levels.
- Model underestimates true volatility in low-price regimes (e.g., <75) — should adjust downward bias in early forecast days.
- Final 5–10 days should be adjusted downward by 1–3% to reflect mean reversion or market correction.
